method: 照片使用 Wikimedia Commons 具体文件；保留实际作者、原文件页和许可，并逐图查看。排除画谱、食物、混合多物种标本板、分辨率不足和身份冲突照片；馆藏、捕获或保存标本保留原说明，不冒充水下活体照。新图使用原尺寸或缩小版本，短边至少256、长边至少500像素；不放大小图。Hypseleotris compressa 原文件500×299，放大细节有限。
分类用 GBIF 精确接受名，原生分布与 FishBase26.06 逐种原文交叉核对，并补充政府、研究机构、原始研究和专家馆藏凭证。旧广义物种、引入鱼、明确灭绝群体及含混同名河流不自动发布。A.arcasii 的旧 Duero/Soria 照片涉及2023年分类拆分且新名无法精确匹配GBIF，已跳过；不把旧照片绑定到修订后的其他鱼种。
明确河名的原始记录直接关联对应流域；少量文献没有河名、但保留专家鉴定及原始坐标的凭证，结合原生范围和GRDC多边形推定流域，标为medium并说明这是地理推断，保留原始地点与精度。采样凭证点和水域展示锚点不会被描述为照片拍摄地。
新增受控的每条关系定位字段，保留坐标来源与说明。Natron鱼使用专家馆藏记载的南岸泉溪[35.91854,-2.59617]，而非高盐湖心；ChewBahir只有流域级Schall记录，未确认淡水地点，撤回不可靠湖面及父流域定位。Puelo的Galaxias maculatus使用原研究点[-72.32,-41.64]，不放到原文排除的LakePuelo。
已核实湖鱼可同时关联其父集水区，但使用原湖泊位置，只表示已知湖内分布，不推成整条主河或全流域占据。本轮如此补足Turkana、Rukwa、Narva/Peipus三个原有空白父集水区。Jordan鱼使用约旦河淡水河段；DeadSea2904表示集水区，不表示鱼生活在死海盐湖。
NASCO公开Atlas仅作为所选具名大西洋鲑河流的事实依据，未重新发布完整原始数据集或形状。原生范围、现代种群风险和孵化场支持是不同概念；未知状态不解释为当前数量，恢复原生群体不解释为新增引入分布；Lost记录及本轮不稳妥的人工维持记录没有加入。冰岛以原始监测报告逐种补充，Lagarfljót棕鳟采用2024年LAGF02原始WGS84湖站坐标。
地球总览每种鱼只有一个稳定的代表水域标记，以减少同种鱼重复堆叠；按水域筛选可查看该水域全部已有来源的鱼，所有核实关联仍保留。水域展示位置与短引导线帮助理解归属，不代表真实采集密度、完整自然边界或全水系可达。
L.idus和B.sapa在Aral父集水区的原始依据具体为Amudar'ya，因此使用NaturalEarth明确阿姆河河线锚点[60.70292,41.67087]；不放到锡尔河侧通用流域中心或干涸咸海。

Australian and New Zealand forms sometimes recognized as subspecies.  Most easily confused with Anguilla obscura and the surest way of distinguishing them is to count the vertebrae.  Reported from Western and American Samoa (Ref. 592).

speciesSources.behaviorSourceText: Adults are found in coastal waters (Ref. 2850, 44894, 57400), often entering estuaries and rivers (Ref. 2847, 3573, 11230, 44894, 57400), sometimes far-up-river, lagoons and hypersaline environments (Ref. 57400); and in mangrove areas (Ref. 138854). They are usually in schools over sand or mud bottom (Ref. 2850), between 0 and 10 m, occurring equally in tropical, subtropical and temperate waters (Project MUGIL).  They are mainly diurnal, feeding on detritus, micro-algae and benthic organisms (Ref. 56548, 74902, 74760).  Juveniles feed on zooplankton until about 3.0 cm SL (Ref. 59043).  Reproduction takes place at sea, at various times of the year depending on the location (Ref. 74907, Amour).  Adults form schools and migrate offshore to spawn and developing larvae migrate back inshore (Ref. 81659). There is absence of an obligatory freshwater phase in the life cycle (Ref. 74752).   Females spawn 0.8 to 2.6 million eggs which develop at sea (Ref. 74912, Chen & Su 1986).  Sexually mature at 3 to 4 years (Ref. 74902).  Maximum length reported as 120 cm SL (Ref. 7399, 57400, 81659) remains to be confirmed (Project MUGIL).  Maximum weight reported as 12 kg (Ref. 56527) seems too high for the area and remains to be confirmed (Project MUGIL).  Widely cultivated in freshwater and brackish ponds (Ref. 2847, Jackson 1984, Liao 1981).  Marketed fresh, dried, salted, and frozen; roe sold fresh or smoked (Ref. 9321); also used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

speciesSources.behaviorSourceText: Occurs in swamps, creeks, and river with lentic waters.  Preys on small invertebrates, particularly the larvae of aquatic insects (Ref. 12225).  Breeds before the start of the rainy season (Ref. 10645) or during the rainy season, with a fecundity count of 6473 eggs (Ref. 10643).  Males persistently defend their territory and apparently make electric signals (by increased electric organ discharge (EOD) rates and interruptions thereof) to females passing by to draw in a spawning partner (Ref. 10605).  Mature females' EODs are of higher frequencies than mature males (Ref. 10645).  Plasma androgens modulate the EOD frequency during the breeding season (Ref. 10767).  Embryos hatch on day 4; larvae begin to feed on day 11.  The electric organ and electroreceptors are both present in the larva at the time of first exogenous feeding (Ref. 10605).  Seems to reach sexual maturity at 1 year of age, based on breeding experiments (Ref. 10011).
